title: CMA secures important changes from Google to tackle fake reviews - GOV.UK

facts.fact: Research cited by the CMA (via Which?) found that 89% of consumers use online customer reviews when researching a product or service.
facts.quote: research has shown that 89% of consumers use online customer reviews when researching a product or service

facts.fact: Under Google's undertakings, businesses found boosting star ratings via fake reviews will have their review function deactivated and cannot receive new reviews.
facts.quote: Businesses will also have their review function deactivated, meaning they cannot receive any new reviews.

facts.fact: Firms that repeatedly engage in fake review activity will have all their reviews deleted for 6 months or more under Google's undertakings.
facts.quote: Those firms that repeatedly engage in fake review activity will have all their reviews deleted for 6 months or more.

facts.fact: Google will report to the CMA over a 3-year period to show compliance with its undertakings.
facts.quote: the firm will report to the CMA over a 3-year period.

facts.fact: The Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 will empower the CMA to fine firms that break consumer law up to 10% of their global turnover.
facts.quote: empower the CMA to fine firms that break the law up to 10% of their global turnover.

facts.fact: The CMA's new consumer powers under the DMCC Act were expected to come into force in April 2025.
facts.quote: When this comes into force (expected in April 2025)

facts.fact: The consultation on the CMA's draft unfair commercial practices guidance concluded on 22 January 2025.
facts.quote: The consultation period on this guidance concluded on 22 January 2025

facts.fact: Google plans to expand its sanctions programme to additional non-UK businesses, including EU businesses, by the end of 2025.
facts.quote: Google plans to expand its sanctions programme to additional non-UK businesses, including EU businesses, by the end of 2025.

facts.fact: The specific business sanctions Google agreed to enforce are fixed for 3 years before Google can modify them.
facts.quote: The specific business sanctions Google has agreed to enforce, as outlined in the undertakings, are fixed for 3 years.
